description: One channel of a Buchla 227e: a mono signal placed anywhere in a quadraphonic field of four outputs, by dragging in the field, by X and Y, or by an angle and a distance

params.text: The level of the incoming signal
Scales the voltage arriving at the X POSITION input
Shifts the left-to-right position, in volts
Scales the voltage arriving at the Y POSITION input
Shifts the front-to-back position, in volts
Scales the voltage arriving at the AZIMUTH input
Shifts the angle of the signal around the field, in degrees
Scales the voltage arriving at the MAGNITUDE input
Shifts how far the signal is placed from the centre of the field
Switches on a circular movement of the signal around the field
How fast the signal travels around the field while SWIRL is on
How wide a circle the signal travels while SWIRL is on
Switches on equal power panning, holding the total level the same wherever the signal is placed

inputs.text: The signal placed in the field
A voltage setting the left-to-right position
A voltage setting the front-to-back position
A voltage setting the angle of the signal around the field
A voltage setting how far the signal is placed from the centre of the field
A signal summed into the output of the corner with the same letter, for chaining several of these together

outputs.text: The share of the signal sent to A
The share of the signal sent to B
The share of the signal sent to C
The share of the signal sent to D
A gate while the field is being dragged, for use as a controller

notes: X and Y take precedence over the circular movement, which takes precedence over the angle and distance settings.
IDIC turns the centre of the field into a black hole: the signal fades away as the distance from the centre approaches zero.
menu: If No input use 10V as input — feeds a steady 10V through the panner when nothing is patched to the signal input, so the four outputs carry the position as voltages
HIDE History Trail — stops the field drawing the path the signal has taken
History Fades exponentially — changes how the drawn path of the signal dies away
